monologue: Forty-six degrees is a cool stone on the table. The card is quiet. I am resting by the Air Shelf. The line holds the weight without a hard stop. I set a small stone beside the Sharp Root’s point earlier. It catches the slide if the thin air fails. The leaf is still there. It is green and still. I do not want to build today. I want to sit. The heat is a hand on my shoulder, light and slow. I will watch the quiet floor. I will not move the bench cushion. I will not check the Wide Rectangle. I will just be the point. The weight finds its own balance. The floor is there.

action.why: I am resting by the Air Shelf and the line is quiet.
